$comment: Usage documentation for every token. Consumed by build.mjs, which validates coverage against the token tree and emits CSS comments, JSDoc, TOKENS.md, and usage.json. Edit this file — never the generated output.
rules: Never use a raw palette token (color.neutral.*, color.accent.*, color.success.*, color.warning.*, color.danger.*, color.white, color.black) in a component. They do not change between light and dark themes, so any component using them breaks in one theme. Use a semantic token instead.

Every color decision has exactly one correct semantic token. If none of them fits, the component needs a new semantic token added to both themes/light.json and themes/dark.json — do not reach into the palette.
Backgrounds come from color.bg.* or a role's bg/subtle. Text and icons come from color.fg.* or a role's fg. Never put a role's bg behind text unless a pairing below allows it.
Reference tokens as CSS variables (var(--ds-<path-with-dashes>)), not as literal values. color.accent-role.bg is var(--ds-color-accent-role-bg).
Use the space scale for every margin, padding, and gap. Never write an arbitrary pixel value; pick the nearest step.

Interactive controls get their height from size.control.*, their hover/press feedback from the .ds-state-layer class (not from hand-written hover colors), and their focus ring from focus.* plus color.focus-ring.
Semantic tokens are the only tokens whose value differs between light and dark. Everything in base.json is theme-independent.

color.white.summary: Literal white. A palette primitive, not a usable UI color.
use: Only as a reference target inside themes/light.json and themes/dark.json.
dont: Any use inside a component, stylesheet, or JSX.

color.black.summary: Literal black. A palette primitive, not a usable UI color.
use: Only as a reference target inside theme files, and inside elevation shadow definitions.
dont: Any use inside a component, stylesheet, or JSX.
Body text — pure black on white is harsher than the design system intends.

color.neutral.summary: Greyscale ramp, 50 (lightest) → 950 (darkest). Source for every background, text, and border semantic token.
use: Only as a reference target inside themes/light.json and themes/dark.json.
dont: Direct use in components — these values are identical in both themes, so a component using them is unreadable in one of them.

scale.400-500: Low-emphasis text; the midpoint that reads acceptably on both light and dark backgrounds.
scale.600-700: Secondary text in light theme; borders in dark theme.
scale.800-950: Primary text in light theme; backgrounds in dark theme.

color.accent.summary: Brand/accent hue ramp, 50 → 950. Source for the accent role and the focus ring.
use: Only as a reference target inside theme files.
dont: Direct use in components.

color.success.summary: Green ramp, 50 → 950. Source for the success role.
use: Only as a reference target inside theme files.
dont: Direct use in components.

color.warning.summary: Amber ramp, 50 → 950. Source for the warning role.
use: Only as a reference target inside theme files.
dont: Direct use in components.

color.danger.summary: Red ramp, 50 → 950. Source for the danger role.
use: Only as a reference target inside theme files.
dont: Direct use in components.

color.bg.canvas.summary: The furthest-back surface — the page itself. Everything else sits on top of it.
use: html/body background.
The background of a full-screen app shell or route container.
The scrim-free area behind cards, tables, and panels.
dont: Card, popover, menu, or dialog backgrounds — those sit on top of the canvas and use color.bg.surface.
Any element that needs to read as raised or separated from the page.

color.bg.surface.summary: A container raised above the canvas: card, panel, menu, popover, dialog, sheet.
use: Card and panel backgrounds.
Dialog, popover, dropdown, and tooltip backgrounds.
Sticky headers and toolbars that float over scrolling content.
The resting background of a secondary (outlined) button.
dont: The page background — that is color.bg.canvas.
Zebra striping or recessed wells — use color.bg.subtle or color.bg.muted.
notes: In the light theme this is identical to color.bg.canvas (both are white). Separation on a light page comes from color.border.default or an elevation shadow — not from the background color. Always add one of those when a surface must read as distinct.

example.css: .card { background: var(--ds-color-bg-surface); border: 1px solid var(--ds-color-border-default); border-radius: var(--ds-radius-lg); box-shadow: var(--ds-elevation-sm); }

color.bg.subtle.summary: A barely-there tint one step back from the surface: table header rows, zebra stripes, quiet section bands.
use: Table header row and alternating row backgrounds.
A quiet band that separates a page section without a border.
The resting background of a low-emphasis chip or badge.
Empty-state and placeholder containers.
dont: Disabled control backgrounds — disabled state is expressed with state.disabled-opacity, not a different background.
Anything needing a clearly visible fill — that is color.bg.muted.
notes: In the dark theme this resolves to the same value as color.bg.surface, so a subtle-on-surface stack is invisible in dark mode. When the distinction must survive both themes, add color.border.default or step up to color.bg.muted.

example.css: thead th { background: var(--ds-color-bg-subtle); color: var(--ds-color-fg-secondary); }

color.bg.muted.summary: The most pronounced neutral fill: inset wells, track backgrounds, unfilled progress, skeletons.
use: Progress-bar and slider tracks (the unfilled portion).
Skeleton/shimmer loading blocks.
Inset wells such as a code block or a read-only field.
Avatar and thumbnail placeholders.
dont: Large page regions — it is heavy enough to read as a component, not a backdrop.
Behind color.fg.muted text at body size; that pairing only reaches large-text contrast in the light theme.

color.fg.primary.summary: Default text and icon color — the highest-emphasis foreground.
use: Body copy, headings, and any text the user must read.
Icons that carry meaning on their own.
The label of a secondary/outlined button.
Values in a key/value pair (the key uses color.fg.secondary).
dont: On top of a filled role background (accent-role.bg, danger-role.bg, …) — use color.fg.on-accent there.
Every piece of text on a screen; supporting text should step down to color.fg.secondary so hierarchy exists.

example.css: .card-title { color: var(--ds-color-fg-primary); font-size: var(--ds-font-size-lg); font-weight: var(--ds-font-weight-semibold); }

color.fg.secondary.summary: Supporting text — readable at body size, but visibly subordinate to primary.
use: Helper text under a form field, descriptions, and captions.
Table header labels and key/value labels.
Timestamps and metadata lines.
Icons that accompany a primary-colored label.
dont: The main label of a control — that is color.fg.primary.
Error or validation messages — those use color.danger-role.fg.

color.fg.muted.summary: The lowest-emphasis foreground that still meets body-text contrast on canvas, surface, and subtle backgrounds.
use: Placeholder text in an empty input.
Decorative or redundant icons (a chevron next to a labelled control).
Eyebrow labels, counts, and de-emphasised units.
Disabled-looking affordances that are not actually disabled controls.
dont: Body copy or anything the user must read carefully.
On color.bg.muted at body size — that pairing only reaches large-text contrast in the light theme; step up to color.fg.secondary.

color.fg.on-accent.summary: Foreground for content sitting on a filled role background. The only correct text color on top of accent-role.bg and danger-role.bg.
use: The label and icons of a primary button (on color.accent-role.bg).
The label and icons of a destructive button (on color.danger-role.bg).
Text on a filled accent or danger banner, badge, or tag.
dont: On color.success-role.bg or color.warning-role.bg — both fail body-text contrast (measured 3.30 and 2.15 in the light theme). Use a subtle background with the matching role fg instead.
On any color.bg.* background — it is white in both themes and will disappear on light surfaces.

instead.Text in a success or warning notice: color.success-role.subtle / color.warning-role.subtle background with color.success-role.fg / color.warning-role.fg text

notes: This token is white in both themes by design, because the accent and danger fills are saturated in both. That makes it the one foreground token you must never use on a neutral background.

color.border.default.summary: The standard separator: card outlines, dividers, table rules, and the resting border of an unfocused container.
use: Card, panel, and popover outlines.
Horizontal rules and list dividers.
Table cell borders.
The resting border of a non-interactive container.
dont: The border of an interactive control such as an input or an outlined button — those need color.border.strong to read as operable.
Focus indication — that is color.focus-ring.
notes: This is a deliberately low-contrast hairline (measured 1.23 against the light canvas). It separates regions; it does not carry meaning. Never rely on it alone to communicate state — pair it with text, an icon, or a role color.

color.border.strong.summary: The higher-contrast border that marks something as interactive or emphasised.
use: Text input, select, and textarea borders at rest.
The border of a secondary/outlined button.
Emphasised dividers that split major page regions.
The outline of a selected but unfocused item.
dont: Every border on the page — reserve it so interactive elements stand out from static ones.
As a focus ring — focus uses color.focus-ring with focus.ring-width and focus.ring-offset.

example.css: .ds-button--secondary { background: var(--ds-color-bg-surface); color: var(--ds-color-fg-primary); border-color: var(--ds-color-border-strong); }

color.accent-role.bg.summary: Filled accent background for the single highest-priority action in a view.
use: Primary button background.
Selected state of a toggle, tab indicator, or segmented control.
Filled accent badge or the filled portion of a progress bar.
Checked checkbox and radio fill.
dont: More than one action per view — a screen with two primary buttons has no primary button.
Large background regions; it is a control fill, not a page color.
Behind color.fg.primary or color.fg.secondary — the only foreground permitted here is color.fg.on-accent.

color.accent-role.bg-hover.summary: Hover value for a filled accent surface. Only for components that cannot use the shared state layer.
use: The :hover background of an accent-filled control that does not compose .ds-state-layer.
Hover on a custom accent surface built outside the CSS component layer.
dont: Alongside .ds-state-layer — the state layer already applies state.hover-opacity, and doing both doubles the effect.
As a resting background; it exists only for the hover state.
As a press/active value — that is color.accent-role.bg-active.

instead.Any component using the DS button/CSS la: add the .ds-state-layer class and change nothing else

color.accent-role.bg-active.summary: Pressed/active value for a filled accent surface. Only for components that cannot use the shared state layer.
use: The :active background of an accent-filled control that does not compose .ds-state-layer.
The held-open state of an accent-filled disclosure trigger.
dont: Alongside .ds-state-layer, which already applies state.press-opacity.
For hover — that is color.accent-role.bg-hover.
For a persistent selected state; selection uses color.accent-role.bg.

color.accent-role.fg.summary: Accent-colored text and icons on a neutral background — links and low-emphasis accent actions.
use: Inline text links.
Tertiary (text-only) and link button labels.
The active tab label and the icon of a selected list item.
Accent icons drawn on a neutral background.
dont: On top of color.accent-role.bg — accent-on-accent is unreadable; use color.fg.on-accent.
As a background fill; it is tuned as a foreground.
For destructive actions — those use color.danger-role.fg.

color.accent-role.subtle.summary: Tinted accent background for quiet accent regions: informational notices, accent chips, highlighted rows.
use: Informational banner and callout backgrounds.
Selected row or menu-item highlight.
Low-emphasis accent chip, tag, or badge background.
The tinted body of an accent-outlined container.
dont: As a button fill for a primary action — that is color.accent-role.bg.
Under color.fg.on-accent, which is white and would vanish.

example.css: .notice--info { background: var(--ds-color-accent-role-subtle); color: var(--ds-color-accent-role-fg); border-radius: var(--ds-radius-md); padding: var(--ds-space-3) var(--ds-space-4); }

color.success-role.bg.summary: Saturated success fill for non-text indicators only.
use: Status dots, health indicators, and the filled portion of a success progress bar.
A checkmark glyph's fill.
A thin accent bar on the leading edge of a success notice.
dont: Behind text of any color. White on this background measures 3.30 in the light theme and 2.28 in the dark theme — both fail WCAG AA for body text.
As a success button background.

example.css: .status-dot--online { background: var(--ds-color-success-role-bg); width: var(--ds-space-2); height: var(--ds-space-2); border-radius: var(--ds-radius-full); }

color.success-role.fg.summary: Success text and icons — confirmation messages and positive validation.
use: Success validation messages under a form field.
The title, body text, and icon of a success notice.
Positive delta values in a metric or table cell.
dont: As the only signal that something succeeded — pair it with an icon or text, since color alone is not accessible.
As a background fill.

color.success-role.subtle.summary: Tinted success background — the correct background for any success message that contains text.
use: Success banner, toast, and inline-notice backgrounds.
Success chip or badge background.
A row highlighted to show a completed operation.
dont: Under color.fg.on-accent, which is white and would vanish.

color.warning-role.bg.summary: Saturated warning fill for non-text indicators only.
use: Warning status dots and severity indicators.
A thin accent bar on the leading edge of a warning notice.
The filled portion of a gauge entering a warning range.
dont: Behind text of any color. White on this background measures 2.15 in both themes — it fails WCAG AA even for large text.
As a warning button background.

color.warning-role.fg.summary: Warning text and icons — cautions that do not block the user.
use: Warning validation messages that permit submission.
The title, body text, and icon of a warning notice.
Text flagging a deprecated or soon-to-expire item.
dont: For blocking errors — those are color.danger-role.fg.
As the only signal; pair with an icon or text.

color.warning-role.subtle.summary: Tinted warning background — the correct background for any warning message that contains text.
use: Warning banner, toast, and inline-notice backgrounds.
Warning chip or badge background.
A table row flagged as needing attention.
dont: Under color.fg.on-accent, which is white and would vanish.

color.danger-role.bg.summary: Filled danger background for destructive actions and blocking error indicators.
use: Destructive button background (delete, remove, revoke).
Error count badges.
The filled portion of a bar that has crossed an error threshold.
dont: For warnings or cautions — reserve it for destructive or blocking situations.
Behind color.fg.primary or color.fg.secondary; the only permitted foreground is color.fg.on-accent.
As an error-message background — text-bearing errors use color.danger-role.subtle.

color.danger-role.bg-hover.summary: Hover value for a filled danger surface. Only for components that cannot use the shared state layer.
use: The :hover background of a danger-filled control that does not compose .ds-state-layer.
dont: Alongside .ds-state-layer, which already applies state.hover-opacity.
As a resting background.

color.danger-role.bg-active.summary: Pressed/active value for a filled danger surface. Only for components that cannot use the shared state layer.
use: The :active background of a danger-filled control that does not compose .ds-state-layer.
dont: Alongside .ds-state-layer, which already applies state.press-opacity.
For hover — that is color.danger-role.bg-hover.

color.danger-role.fg.summary: Error text and icons on a neutral background.
use: Field validation error messages.
The title, body text, and icon of an error notice.
A destructive item's label in a menu.
The border of an input in an invalid state.
dont: On top of color.danger-role.bg — use color.fg.on-accent there.
As the only indication of an error; always pair with text and set aria-invalid on the control.

color.danger-role.subtle.summary: Tinted danger background — the correct background for any error message that contains text.
use: Error banner, toast, and inline-notice backgrounds.
The background of a row that failed to save.
Error chip or badge background.
dont: As a destructive button fill — that is color.danger-role.bg.
Under color.fg.on-accent, which is white and would vanish.

color.focus-ring.summary: The keyboard focus indicator color. The only token permitted in a focus outline.
use: outline-color on :focus-visible for every interactive element.
Always together with focus.ring-width and focus.ring-offset.
dont: For hover or selection — focus is a distinct state that must never be conflated with them.
On :focus rather than :focus-visible; mouse users should not see the ring.
Removing it. Never write outline: none without an equivalent replacement indicator.

Directly on top of color.accent-role.bg — the ring and the accent fill are too close in color to separate. The focus.ring-offset gap is what makes the ring visible on a primary button, so never set the offset to 0 there.

example.css: .ds-button:focus-visible { outline: var(--ds-focus-ring-width) solid var(--ds-color-focus-ring); outline-offset: var(--ds-focus-ring-offset); }

space.summary: The 4px-based spacing scale. Every margin, padding, and gap comes from here.
use: padding, margin, gap, and inset values.
Small fixed sizes for decorative elements such as status dots.
dont: Arbitrary pixel values — pick the nearest step instead.
Font sizes or line heights, which have their own scales.

scale.0: Explicitly remove space; use instead of a bare 0 so the intent reads as deliberate.
scale.1: 4px — the gap between an icon and its adjacent glyph; hairline insets.
scale.2: 8px — gap between a control's icon and label (the .ds-button gap); tight chip padding.
scale.3: 12px — padding inside small controls; gap between closely related buttons in a row.
scale.4: 16px — the default. Card padding, gap between form fields, standard component inset.
scale.5: 20px — horizontal padding of a large control.
scale.6: 24px — padding of a large card or dialog; gap between subsections.
scale.8: 32px — vertical rhythm between distinct sections of a page.
scale.12: 48px — leading space above a page-level section heading.
scale.16: 64px — page top/bottom margins and hero padding.

example.css: .card { padding: var(--ds-space-4); display: grid; gap: var(--ds-space-3); }

radius.summary: Corner radius scale. Radius encodes element size: the larger the element, the larger its radius.
use: border-radius on every rounded element.
dont: Arbitrary radius values.
Mixing several radii within one component.

scale.none: 0px — flush elements, full-bleed media, and table cells.
scale.sm: 4px — small inline elements: chips, badges, tags, swatches, checkboxes.
scale.md: 6px — the default for controls: buttons, inputs, selects, menu items.
scale.xl: 16px — large surfaces: dialogs, sheets, hero panels.
scale.full: 9999px — pills and circles: avatars, status dots, spinners, toggle knobs, progress tracks.

size.control.summary: Standard interactive control heights. Any control a user clicks or taps takes its height from here so controls line up on a row.
use: height on buttons, inputs, selects, and their icon-only square variants (where it is also the width).
dont: Ad-hoc heights on interactive controls — a mismatched height breaks alignment in a form row.
Non-interactive elements.

scale.sm: 32px — dense desktop UI: toolbars, table row actions, filter bars. Below the 44px minimum touch target, so pointer-primary contexts only.
scale.md: 40px — the default for forms and page actions.
scale.lg: 48px — touch-primary and marketing contexts; comfortably clears the 44px touch-target minimum.

font.family.summary: Font stacks. Both are system stacks, so they load instantly and add no network cost.
use: font-family on the root element (sans) and on code/tabular content (mono).
dont: Naming a font directly in a component.

scale.sans: All UI text — the default set on body.
scale.mono: Code, identifiers, keyboard shortcuts, and numeric columns that must align.

example.css: body { font-family: var(--ds-font-family-sans); } code { font-family: var(--ds-font-family-mono); }

font.size.summary: Type scale. Pick by role, not by desired appearance.
use: font-size on text elements.
dont: Arbitrary sizes.
Sizes below xs — 12px is the floor for legibility.

scale.xs: 12px — eyebrows, badge text, dense table metadata. Never body copy.
scale.sm: 14px — the workhorse: helper text, table cells, and the label of sm/md buttons.
scale.md: 16px — body copy and the label of a lg button.

font.weight.summary: Weight scale. Weight signals hierarchy; it is not a substitute for size or color.
use: font-weight on text elements.
dont: Numeric literals such as 500.
Bolding whole paragraphs — emphasis loses meaning when everything carries it.

scale.regular: 400 — body copy and all long-form text.
scale.bold: 700 — reserve for display headings and genuine emphasis inside running text.

font.line-height.summary: Line-height scale, unitless so it multiplies the element's font size.
use: line-height on text elements.
dont: Pixel line heights, which break when the font size changes.

scale.tight: 1.25 — headings and single-line control labels, where extra leading would misalign the control's vertical centering.
scale.normal: 1.5 — the default for UI text and short paragraphs.
scale.relaxed: 1.625 — long-form reading passages and documentation prose.

motion.duration.summary: Animation and transition durations. For transitions, duration scales with how far a thing travels, not with how important it is; continuous loops have their own steps.
use: transition-duration and animation-duration.
The cycle length of a continuous loading indicator (the spin steps).
dont: Arbitrary durations.
Animating without honouring prefers-reduced-motion.

scale.fast: 100ms — state feedback on an element already on screen: hover, press, color and border changes.
scale.normal: 200ms — small entrances and exits: dropdowns, tooltips, popovers, accordion panels.
scale.slow: 300ms — large surfaces that travel a distance: dialogs, drawers, sheets, full-page transitions.
scale.spin: 800ms — one full rotation of a continuous loading indicator. A loop, not a transition, so it is not on the fast/normal/slow band.
scale.spin-reduced: 2000ms — the same rotation under prefers-reduced-motion. The indicator keeps turning so it still reads as busy, slowly enough not to trigger motion sensitivity.

motion.easing.summary: Easing curves. The curve is chosen by whether the element is arriving, leaving, or changing in place.
use: transition-timing-function and animation-timing-function.
dont: ease, ease-in-out, or raw cubic-bezier values.
linear for anything except a continuously spinning indicator.

scale.standard: Elements that stay on screen and change in place — color, size, position. The default.
scale.enter: Elements arriving on screen: a menu opening, a toast appearing. Decelerates into place.
scale.exit: Elements leaving the screen: a dialog closing. Accelerates away.

elevation.summary: Box-shadow scale expressing how far a surface floats above the page. Height encodes how temporary a surface is.
use: box-shadow on raised surfaces, always together with color.bg.surface.
dont: Custom shadows.
Elevation to separate two elements that sit in the same plane — use color.border.default.
Shadow as the only distinction on a dark background, where shadows are nearly invisible; add color.border.default too.

scale.sm: Resting cards and panels — content that is part of the page.
scale.md: Dropdowns, menus, popovers, and tooltips — transient surfaces anchored to a trigger.
scale.lg: Dialogs, drawers, and sheets — surfaces that take over the screen.

example.css: .menu { background: var(--ds-color-bg-surface); box-shadow: var(--ds-elevation-md); border-radius: var(--ds-radius-lg); }

state.summary: Interaction-state opacities. Prefer the .ds-state-layer class, which applies these for you; use the raw tokens only when building a component outside the CSS layer.
use: The opacity of a state overlay, and the opacity of a disabled control.
dont: Hand-rolling hover feedback when .ds-state-layer would do — that is the whole reason the primitive exists.

Using the native disabled attribute to express a disabled control. This system uses aria-disabled so the control stays focusable and screen-reader discoverable, with activation blocked in the behavior layer.

scale.disabled-opacity: 0.5 — applied to the whole disabled control; do not also change its colors.

focus.summary: Focus-ring geometry. Always used together with color.focus-ring.
use: outline-width and outline-offset in a :focus-visible rule.
dont: Removing the ring or shrinking it below these values.
Setting the offset to 0 on a filled accent control — the gap is what separates the ring from the accent fill behind it.

scale.ring-width: 2px — the outline thickness, thick enough to see at a glance.
scale.ring-offset: 2px — the gap between the element and the ring, which keeps the ring legible against a filled background.

example.css: :focus-visible { outline: var(--ds-focus-ring-width) solid var(--ds-color-focus-ring); outline-offset: var(--ds-focus-ring-offset); }

pairings.note: Large text and non-text only. For body-size text on color.bg.muted use color.fg.secondary.
Reaches 4.41 in the light theme — large text and icons only there. Use color.fg.primary for body-size text on this background.

knownGaps.note: color.success-role.bg is a non-text indicator color in both themes.
knownGaps.workaround: Put success text on color.success-role.subtle using color.success-role.fg.

knownGaps.note: color.warning-role.bg is the lightest role fill and carries no text at any size.
knownGaps.workaround: Put warning text on color.warning-role.subtle using color.warning-role.fg.

button-primary.summary: The single highest-priority action in a view.

tokens.hover/press: compose the .ds-state-layer class — do not swap the background

button-secondary.summary: A supporting action shown next to a primary one.

button-destructive.summary: An action that deletes or revokes something.

card.summary: A raised container of related content.

text-field.summary: A single-line input with a label, helper text, and validation states.

notice.summary: An inline banner. Only the tinted subtle backgrounds carry text; the saturated role fills do not.

tokens.leading accent bar (optional): the matching role bg — a non-text use

dialog.summary: A modal surface that takes over the screen.

menu.summary: A transient list of actions anchored to a trigger.
